description: The mathematics of measuring, compressing and protecting information, from entropy and channel capacity to the codes inside mobile networks and storage. Students compute information measures, build compressors and encoders, and simulate noisy channels to measure error rates against theoretical limits.
modelledOn: Cover and Thomas, Elements of Information Theory
Lin and Costello, Error Control Coding
MacKay, Information Theory, Inference, and Learning Algorithms
outcomes: Compute entropy, conditional entropy and mutual information for discrete sources and channels.
Design and analyse prefix, Huffman, arithmetic and dictionary codes and compare them with the entropy bound.
Derive and compute the capacity of binary and Gaussian channels, and interpret the Shannon limit for real links.
Encode and decode linear block, cyclic and convolutional codes, including syndrome and trellis decoding.
Implement CRC and simulate bit error rate curves to measure coding gain.
Explain how turbo, LDPC and polar codes approach capacity and where they are used.

units.title: Information measures
topics: Self-information, surprisal and the bit as a unit of uncertainty
Entropy of a discrete source; binary entropy function; bounds and properties
Joint and conditional entropy; the chain rule
Mutual information and relative entropy (KL divergence)
Data processing inequality and Fano's inequality
Typical sequences and the asymptotic equipartition property

units.title: Source coding and compression
topics: Prefix codes, the Kraft inequality and the source coding theorem
Huffman coding and its optimality
Entropy of English and Markov sources; entropy rate
Shannon-Fano and arithmetic coding
Dictionary and run-length methods: LZ77, LZW and RLE
Lossy compression: quantisation, rate-distortion idea and transform coding

units.title: Channels and capacity
topics: Discrete memoryless channels; the binary symmetric and binary erasure channels
Channel capacity and the noisy-channel coding theorem
Computing capacity numerically with an iterative algorithm
Gaussian channel, the Shannon-Hartley theorem and the Eb/N0 Shannon limit
Capacity and modulation: bits per symbol, SNR and rural mobile link budgets

units.title: Linear block codes
topics: Error detection and correction; Hamming distance and minimum distance
Generator and parity-check matrices; systematic form
Syndrome decoding and the standard array
Hamming codes and extended Hamming codes
Code bounds: Singleton, Hamming (sphere-packing) and Gilbert-Varshamov

units.title: Cyclic codes, CRC and Reed-Solomon codes
topics: Finite fields: GF(2) and GF(2^m) arithmetic
Cyclic codes: generator polynomial and encoding by polynomial division
CRC: standard polynomials, burst-error detection and LFSR hardware
BCH codes and the idea of multiple-error correction
Reed-Solomon codes and their use in QR codes, storage and broadcast

units.title: Convolutional codes and Viterbi decoding
topics: Convolutional encoders: constraint length, generator polynomials and state diagrams
Trellis diagrams and free distance
Maximum-likelihood decoding with the Viterbi algorithm: path metrics, survivors and traceback
Soft decisions, quantisation and coding gain
Puncturing and rate matching in mobile standards

units.title: Modern codes and coding in practice
topics: Turbo codes and iterative decoding
LDPC codes, Tanner graphs and belief propagation
Polar codes and channel polarisation
Fountain codes and network coding for lossy links
Coding in 4G and 5G, satellite links and storage systems

schedule.title: Surprise, entropy and conditional entropy
schedule.exercise: Compute the entropy of a fair die, a loaded die and the letters of a short Twi sentence, then verify the chain rule H(X,Y) = H(X) + H(Y|X) on a 3x3 joint table.

tasks.title: Compute the entropy of a loaded die and a fair die from their probability tables and plot the binary entropy function for p from 0 to 1
Compute joint, marginal and conditional entropies from a 3x3 joint probability table and verify the chain rule numerically
Write a program that estimates the entropy of a text file from letter frequencies, and compare English, Twi and random text of equal length

schedule.title: Mutual information and typicality
schedule.exercise: Compute mutual information and KL divergence for two small distributions, and show with a Bernoulli source that most long sequences fall in a typical set of size about 2^(nH).

tasks.title: Compute I(X;Y) and the KL divergence D(p||q) for given discrete distributions and check that both are non-negative
Simulate long Bernoulli sequences and measure the fraction falling in the typical set as n grows from 10 to 1000
Build a two-stage noisy chain X to Y to Z, compute I(X;Y) and I(X;Z), and verify the data processing inequality on ten random channels

schedule.title: Prefix codes and Huffman coding
schedule.exercise: Check Kraft's inequality for three candidate length sets, build the Huffman code for a six-symbol source and compare its average length with the entropy; estimate the entropy rate of a two-state Markov source.

tasks.title: Test whether five sets of codeword lengths satisfy the Kraft inequality and say which can form a prefix code
Build a Huffman tree step by step for a six-symbol source and compute its average length and efficiency against the entropy
Estimate the entropy rate of a text from first, second and third order Markov models and compare it with the Huffman average length per letter

schedule.title: Arithmetic, dictionary and lossy compression
schedule.exercise: Arithmetic-code a short message by hand, run LZ77 and LZW on a repeated string, and quantise a sampled sine wave at 2, 4 and 8 bits to see the distortion trade-off.

tasks.title: Trace LZW compression of a 20-character string, listing the dictionary growth and the output codes at each step
Implement an arithmetic coder with exact fractions for a four-symbol source and decode a ten-symbol message back correctly
Quantise a sampled signal at 2, 4 and 8 bits, plot the rate against mean squared error, and compare with the theoretical rate-distortion curve

schedule.title: Channel models and the capacity theorem
schedule.exercise: Derive the capacity of the binary symmetric channel and the binary erasure channel, and compute the capacity of a given asymmetric channel with an iterative algorithm.

tasks.title: Plot the capacity of the binary symmetric channel against its crossover probability and mark the points where capacity is 0 and 1 bit
Compute mutual information of a binary channel for input probabilities from 0 to 1 and locate the capacity-achieving input distribution
Implement the iterative capacity algorithm for a 3-input, 3-output channel, show convergence per iteration and check it against a grid search

schedule.title: Gaussian channels and real links
schedule.exercise: Use the Shannon-Hartley formula to find the maximum rate of a 200 kHz channel at several SNRs, and judge whether a rural 4G link at a given SNR is near its capacity.

tasks.title: Compute and plot channel capacity against SNR in dB for a 200 kHz bandwidth, and read off the SNR needed for 1 Mbit/s
Derive the minimum Eb/N0 as the code rate approaches zero from the capacity formula and mark the value of about -1.59 dB on a plot
Given a rural link budget, compute SNR per distance, the Shannon capacity and the rate of each modulation mode, and report the efficiency gap

schedule.title: Linear block codes and syndrome decoding
schedule.exercise: Find the minimum distance of a small code by listing codewords, build the generator and parity-check matrices of a (6,3) code, and decode three received words using syndromes.

tasks.title: List all codewords of a (5,2) code, find its minimum distance and state how many errors it can detect and correct
Derive the parity-check matrix H from a systematic generator matrix G for a (6,3) code and verify that G times the transpose of H is zero
Implement syndrome decoding with a lookup table for a (7,4) code, then correct every single-bit error pattern and report any miscorrections

schedule.title: Hamming codes and code bounds
schedule.exercise: Encode and correct a Hamming(7,4) word, add an overall parity bit for double-error detection, and test which of three proposed codes violate the Singleton and sphere-packing bounds.

tasks.title: Build a Hamming(7,4) encoder from XOR gates and verify all 16 data words against the expected codewords
Extend Hamming(7,4) with an overall parity bit, inject single and double errors, and tabulate which are corrected and which are only detected
Check the Singleton and sphere-packing bounds for ten parameter sets (n, k, d), identify perfect codes, and plot the best possible rates

schedule.title: Finite fields and cyclic codes
schedule.exercise: Build the multiplication table of GF(8), encode a message with a cyclic (7,4) code by polynomial division, and compute a CRC-8 for a short frame by hand.

tasks.title: Construct GF(8) from a primitive polynomial and fill in its addition and multiplication tables, checking that every nonzero element has an inverse
Encode all 16 messages with a cyclic (7,4) code from its generator polynomial and verify each codeword has zero remainder when divided
Implement a bitwise CRC-16 and check that it detects all single-bit errors, all burst errors up to 16 bits and a measured share of random errors

schedule.title: BCH and Reed-Solomon codes
schedule.exercise: Explain how a Reed-Solomon code over GF(256) corrects burst errors, and compute how many damaged symbols a (255,223) code can repair in a scratched storage block.

tasks.title: Compute the error-correcting capability and rate of RS(255,223) and RS(255,239) and compare how many symbol errors each can repair
Encode a message with a small BCH code from its generator polynomial and correct two injected bit errors with the decoder
Implement a small Reed-Solomon encoder and erasure decoder over GF(16), then recover a message after dropping the maximum number of symbols

schedule.title: Convolutional encoders and trellis decoding
schedule.exercise: Encode a bit stream with the rate-1/2, constraint length 3 code (7,5), draw its state diagram and trellis, and decode a received sequence with two errors using the Viterbi algorithm.

tasks.title: Step through the encoder of the rate-1/2 (7,5) convolutional code for a 6-bit message and record the state and output at each step
Run the Viterbi algorithm on a trellis for a received 12-bit sequence with two errors, listing path metrics and the traceback path
Compute the free distance of a given convolutional code by searching its state diagram and use it to predict the guaranteed correction capability

schedule.title: Soft decisions, coding gain and puncturing
schedule.exercise: Compare hard and soft decision decoding of the same code over an AWGN channel at several Eb/N0 values and estimate the coding gain at a bit error rate of 1e-5.

tasks.title: Plot the theoretical BPSK bit error rate against Eb/N0 and read off the SNR needed for an error rate of 1e-5
Simulate a convolutional code with hard and soft Viterbi decoding over an AWGN channel for six Eb/N0 values and plot both BER curves
Puncture a rate-1/2 code to rates 2/3 and 3/4, decode with the matching pattern and quantify the BER penalty for each increase in rate

schedule.title: Turbo, LDPC, polar and fountain codes
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page comparison of turbo, LDPC and polar codes for a 5G link, a satellite broadcast and a flash-memory controller, and trace one round of belief propagation on a small Tanner graph.

tasks.title: Draw the Tanner graph of a small parity-check matrix, flip one received bit and follow one round of message passing between variable and check nodes
Simulate an LT fountain code for 100 packets over a 20 percent loss link and report how many received packets are needed for full recovery
Build a rate-1/3 parallel concatenated code from two short convolutional encoders and measure how BER changes over five decoding iterations
